chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: O Abu 'Ubaydah! Do not neglect establishing prayers in the Mosque of Kufah even if you have to crawl to it, for establishing one prayer there is equal to establishing seventy prayers in other mosques.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Mosque of Kufah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) exhorts Abu 'Ubaydah not to neglect praying in the Mosque of Kufah, emphasizing its high merit by stating that one prayer there is equivalent to seventy prayers in other mosques, even if one must crawl to reach it. This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual significance of Kufah as a center of Imamate and resistance, linking the physical act of worship to the historical legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt. The hyperbolic reward underscores the unique status of this location in Shia devotional geography, encouraging perseverance in visiting and praying there despite hardship.
